full_judgment: 17. It further appears from the impugned judgment that the learned appellate court below found that the suit plot No. 393 of C.S. khatian No. 261 of mouza Fatullah comprising an area of 1.10 decimals of land originally belonged to Sonaton Baroi alone and this finding of the appellate court below is based on c.s. Khatian No. 261 exhibit 3C in respect of the suit plot No. 393 which speaks that the suit land belonged to Sonaton Baroi alone as a “রায়তী স্থিতিবান”. The learned trial court found that the land recorded in c.s. khatian No. 261 belonged to Sonaton Baroi and Ramananda Baroi in equal shares and the learned appellate court below has reversed that finding observing that in exhibit 3C there is no mentioned that Ramananda Baroi is also 8 annas owner of that jote but this finding of the appellate court below cannot be sustained in law inasmuch as exhibit 3C the c.s. Khatian No. 261 itself shows that Sonaton Baroi and others are the owners and in the column of rent it is written ১৫৯ নং মৌজায় ৭৬ নং খতিয়ানে মোট ৭ ।।৯ পাই Exhibit 3B the c.s. khatian 76 shows that Sonaton Baroi and Ramananda Baroi are the owners of the land recorded in that khatian. Of course, in khatian No. 76 plot No. 83 is recorded whereas the suit plot is recorded in C.S. Khatian No. 261. It is submitted by Mr. Miah Abdul Gafur, the learned Advocate for the plaintiff petitioner, that বরাত mean reference and by referring to the relevant provisions of Technical Rules and Instructions of the Settlement Department, 1957 it has been shown that when tenant have land in different plots in different mouzas the full rent should be entered in one khatian only and cross-reference should be made in all the khatian and as such in the instant case the c.s. Khatian No. 76 and c.s. khatian 261 is to be read together and treated as one document and from this the trial court rightly arrived at a finding that Sonaton Baroi and Ramananda Baroi were equal sharer of the said jote. He has referred to the definition of "jote" as contained in section 5 of the Bengal Tenancy Act. "Jote' does not necessarily mean the interest of a cultivator, or an occupancy holding; it is only a general term and may mean a raiyati, under raiyati or any sort of holding for the purpose of cultivation. It simply connotes a tenancy. So if exhibit 3B and 3C are considered together it appears that the finding of the trial court is at least correct with regard to the prima facie title of the predecessor in interest46of the plaintiff petitioner in the suit land and the observation of the learned appellate court below cannot be maintained in view of the fact that in arriving at such a finding that Sonaton Baroi is the sole owner of the c.s. Khatian No. 393 is based on misreading of exhibit 3B as well as 3C because in exhibit 3C itself in column of owner it is written "owner is Sonaton Baroi and others and in the column of rent it is written “১৫৯ নং মৌজায় ৭৬ নং খতিয়ানে মোট ৭ ।।৯ পাই ” and the learned appellate court has failed to take notice of the contents of exhibit 3C and 3B and totally misread exhibit 3C and therefore the finding of the learned appellate Court below that Sonaton Baroi is the Sole owner of the suit land is absolutely contrary to the materials and evidence on record. At least there is prima facie evidence to show that both Sonatan Baroi and Ramananda were 8 annas share of the land recorded in 2 Khatians namely C. S. Khatian No. 261 and 76. On top of that the R.S. Khatian also stand in the name of the plaintiff petitioner. It is submitted that this R.S. Khatian has been published in the year 1974 in the district of Narayanganj by virtue of section 144 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. This RS. Khatian also has a presumptive value and this R.S. Khatian has been published after conducting field survey. In that view of the matter also it can be said that the plaintiff petitioner has been able to prove his prima facie title and possession in the suit land. If these 3 documents are considered along with the oral evidence of all the P.Ws. and D.Ws. it appears that the finding of the trial court that the plaintiff has been able to prove her prima facie title and exclusive possession in the suit land cannot be assailed. I, thus, find that the finding of the appellate court below that C.S. plot No. 393 entirely belonged to Sonatan Baroi is erroneous and contrary to the materials and evidence on record.
